title: Testing the Spirits
definition: The doctrine of Testing the Spirits teaches that believers must test spiritual claims by whether they confess the true Christ and agree with apostolic truth.
summary: Testing the Spirits names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. believers must test spiritual claims by whether they confess the true Christ and agree with apostolic truth. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Testing the Spirits because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: believers must test spiritual claims by whether they confess the true Christ and agree with apostolic truth. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because deception often enters through voices that sound spiritual but lower, replace, or distort Jesus. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not be impressed by spiritual language alone. Ask what is being said about Christ, the Gospel, holiness, and Scripture. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
